title: Whisky From Japan
subtitle: But not Japanese whisky: Hakata, from the Hikari Distillery in Fukuoka
description: How whisky came to Japan, from Perry's ships to Torii, Taketsuru and Rita, the 2021 standard that defined Japanese whisky, and the boom that made it necessary. Then the turn: the glass the room has been drinking since slide 2 is Hakata, made in Fukuoka from Kyushu barley with koji instead of malt, aged in sherry casks, and sold in America as whisky from Japan because it cannot be called Japanese whisky. Three pours from one distillery: the 10, 12 and 16 Year.
tags: japanese whisky, koji, shochu, sherry cask, labeling, history, world whisky

pours.name: Hakata 10 Year Sherry Cask
pours.origin: Hikari Distillery (Hikari Shuzo), Hakata-ku, Fukuoka, Japan
pours.style: Barley whisky made with koji: one third koji barley, two thirds unmalted barley; single distilled; aged in ex-oloroso sherry casks
pours.notes: Poured on slide 2 and drunk through the history before the room learns what it is. The koji is loudest here.
